author: Eustathius of Antioch
occasion: Eustathius thanks Constantine for ending idolatry and establishing freedom for the faithful, and urges him to protect the Church from heretics in general who would dishonor any person of the Trinity; Arius is later identified as the specific present threat.
argument: Eustathius praises God for giving Constantine earthly rule and for abolishing idolatry through him, so that the world is now illumined by the knowledge of God and the consubstantial Trinity is proclaimed. He urges the emperor to guard this faith as a wall and to allow no heretic to dishonor any person of the Trinity. He identifies Arius as the source of the present disturbance, calling him 'the namesake of the madness' (ὁ τῆς μανίας ἐπώνυμος), accusing him of denying that the only-begotten Son and Word is consubstantial with the Father and of numbering the Creator with creation, calling him 'worshipper of the created' (ὁ κτιστολάτρης). Finally, he asks Constantine either to persuade Arius to abandon his errors or, if he persists, to remove him from the Church so that his muddy sophistry cannot ensnare simpler souls.

outline.move: Thanksgiving to God and praise of Constantine for ending idolatry and establishing the proclamation of the consubstantial Trinity.
Exhortation to Constantine to guard this faith as a wall and prevent any heretic from dishonoring one person of the Trinity.
Identification of Arius as 'the namesake of the madness' and cause of the disturbance, and statement of his errors concerning the Son's consubstantiality and the Creator's relation to creation.
Appeal to Constantine either to persuade Arius to repent or to expel him from the Church to protect the simple.

cast.who: The author, speaking in first-person plural on behalf of the orthodox faithful; his episcopal title is not stated in the fragment.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ταύτῃ τειχίζεται, βασιλεῦ, τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας σου κράτος· ταύτην ἡμῖν ἄσυλον διαφύλαττε.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The first-person plural forms (ἡμῖν, ἡμῶν) appear in contexts that include Eustathius with the faithful/orthodox community, not as self-reference alone. The brief should note these plural forms represent the orthodox 'we' (Eustathius speaking on behalf of the Church), and should also include "Εὐχαριστοῦμεν" as a first-person plural marker of Eustathius's voice in frag-open.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Arius, 'who': 'An Alexandrian presbyter, described as 'the namesake of the madness' (ὁ τῆς μανίας ἐπώνυμος), whose teaching denies the Son's consubstantiality with the Father.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὃς, ὡς οὐκ ἴσμεν ὅπως, τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ τῆς Ἀλεξανδρέων ἐγκαταλεγεὶς Ἐκκλησίας
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source states Arius was 'enrolled in the presbyterate of the Alexandrian Church' (τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ...ἐγκαταλεγεὶς), which is more specific than 'an Alexandrian presbyter'—it indicates he was enrolled/listed in the presbyterate, with the implication this was done in a way Eustathius finds questionable (ὡς οὐκ ἴσμεν ὅπως, 'we know not how').

_unresolved_facts.claim: calling him 'worshipper of the created' (ὁ κτιστολάτρης)
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τῇ κτίσει τὸν κτίστην ὁ κτιστολάτρης συναριθμεῖν ἐπείγεται
_unresolved_facts.fix: The term κτιστολάτρης is a compound of κτίστης (creator) and λάτρης (worshipper), meaning 'worshipper of the creator' or more precisely in context, one who worships the Creator as if he were a creature/by numbering him with creation. The brief's gloss 'worshipper of the created' inverts the meaning; it should be 'worshipper of the Creator [as creature]' or 'one who worships the Creator [among creatures]' or simply transliterated with explanation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: if he persists, to remove him from the Church
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἢ τοῖς ἐν οἷς ἑάλω κακοδοξίας ἐγκείμενον ἀσεβήμασιν, ἄρδην τῆς Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἀφανίσειας ἐπαύλεως
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Greek says 'utterly erase him from the fold of Christ and us' (ἄρδην...ἀφανίσειας), which is stronger than 'remove him from the Church'—it means to destroy/obliterate him from the Christian community. 'Ἐπαυλεως' (fold/enclosure) is also more specific than 'Church'; it is a pastoral metaphor for the sheepfold.

_unresolved_facts.claim: frag-rem-close: 'Appeal to Constantine either to persuade Arius to repent or to expel him from the Church to protect the simple.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τοῦτον ἂν πείσειας, αὐτοκράτωρ, μεταφρονοῦντα, τοῖς ἀποστολικοῖς μὴ ἀντιτείνειν διδάγμασιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The condition is 'if you should persuade him, as one who has changed his mind (μεταφρονοῦντα), not to oppose apostolic teachings'—the persuasion is to a state of having changed his mind, not merely 'to repent.' And the alternative is stronger: 'utterly erase/destroy him from the fold' (ἄρδην ἀφανίσειας), not merely 'expel.'
